clue.text: Essayist beginning to draft a letter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

blocks.note: Charles Lamb, the English essayist who wrote as Elia
the opening letter of draft
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is just starting to draft a letter to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence being drafted, but it is the Greek letter LAMBDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, so it is one alphabetic symbol.

clue.text: In carnival, a certain group of stars

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of carnival, all of a and the start of certain

explanation.surface: At a carnival, a particular band of star performers appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' suggests celebrities at a carnival, but it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerta, the Lizard, is a small northern constellation, a named cluster of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Comes across certain foods in broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the spelling follows the sound

blocks.note: beef, pork and lamb are meats

explanation.surface: A viewer stumbles on some particular foods in a TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to encounter them, as when one comes across them by chance.

clue.text: Grass turns up to be probed by detectives – that settles things

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top
to be probed is to have something pushed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: An informer goes over to the police and is questioned by detectives in a case-closing moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the British slang for an informer, but it is the plant. Detectives go inside the reversed grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is the final game or goal that determines the result, so it settles matters.

clue.text: Bishop blessing one at the pet service?

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a blessing is something valuable to have, an asset

explanation.surface: A bishop gives his blessing to the animals at a church service for pets.
explanation.walkthrough: Some churches hold services where pets are blessed; a basset is a short-legged hound that might be brought along.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a breed of dog, an example of an animal taken to a blessing of pets.

clue.text: Capital city surmounted by gold stars

indicators.note: in a down clue, being surmounted means having something placed on top, so it is written first

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A capital whose skyline is topped by golden stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriga, the Charioteer, is a northern constellation, a pattern formed by bright stars.

clue.text: Flight path keeps going round it

definitions.text: Flight path keeps going round it

blocks.clueFragment: Flight path keeps going round it
blocks.note: surface reading: an aircraft's route keeps circling something, like a plane in a holding pattern

blocks.clueFragment: Flight path keeps going round it
blocks.note: setter's reading: a flight of steps winds round a vertical shaft in a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft circling an airport, but it is a flight of stairs spiralling round the space that holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the shaft in a building where a staircase climbs, often winding around an open centre.

clue.text: Time after time goddess of youth's No. 1

indicators.note: after says the first-named item is placed behind what follows it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth, plus the possessive s
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Again and again, the goddess of youth comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' reads as 'repeatedly', but it is two separate time abbreviations, one placed after the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one means the top or finest, the one rated above all others.

clue.text: Supporting friend taking hold of the dream for now

indicators.note: taking hold of something means gripping it inside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a vision is a dream or imagined sight
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A supportive friend backs someone's dream for the present.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporting word and the friend are joined, and together they hold the dream between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisionally means temporarily, pending something permanent, which is what 'for now' says.

clue.text: Fighter going by Circle Line

blocks.note: a circle has the shape of the letter O
Che Guevara, the revolutionary guerrilla fighter

explanation.surface: A fighter travels on the Circle Line of the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle Line' reads as one London Tube line, but Circle gives a letter and Line is the definition. The circle letter comes first, beside the fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line on the floor behind which a darts player must stand to throw.

clue.text: One maybe looking at club's IT device

blocks.note: first meaning: a fortune teller who reads playing cards, clubs being one suit
second meaning: a machine that reads data from a bank or swipe card

explanation.surface: Somebody examining a club's computer equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Club looks like a society owning an IT device, but it is the card suit, so one looking at clubs reads cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller reading cards and a gadget scanning plastic cards share the same two-word name.

clue.text: Some of the French are about to be eliminated

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined words are read from the end back to the start

blocks.note: des is French for 'some of the'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Part of the French population is about to be wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of the' looks like a partial selection from 'the French', but the whole phrase translates into French as des.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erased has been rubbed out or removed completely, so it is eliminated.

clue.text: Fluctuations in very small silver sign

blocks.note: very is abbreviated, made small, to V
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Tiny movements in some small silver symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are unpredictable changes or whims, so they are erratic ups and downs.

clue.text: Repeated prohibition is applied to male for bad behaviour

indicators.note: repeated says the word that follows is written down twice in a row

blocks.note: a bar is a ban, given twice
is taken as written; applied to places it next
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man keeps getting banned for behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarism is savage or uncivilised conduct, a strong term for very bad behaviour.

clue.text: Somehow strengthened, a bed is not falling apart

indicators.note: something falling apart loses its shape, so these letters break up and re-form

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A rickety bed has been reinforced in some way, yet it is not coming to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word could be taken as the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: the fortification is of a particular kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastioned means fortified with bastions, projecting defensive works, so it is reinforced in a particular way.

clue.text: First appearance not top-class – a liability!

indicators.note: not means without, so the following item is taken away

blocks.note: a debut is someone's first public appearance
U is the old British label for upper-class, top-drawer

explanation.surface: A first performance that is below the best is a liability.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper class in old British slang, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, which an accountant would list as a liability.

clue.text: My children's hospital initially

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: the initials of Great Ormond Street Hospital, the famous London children's hospital

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of their own child's hospital, giving just its initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an interjection of astonishment the word is a mild substitute for an oath, just like 'My!'.

clue.text: City girl trailing after family member

indicators.note: trailing after something means coming behind it, so this word is placed second

blocks.note: a gran is a grandmother
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A city girl follows a relative around.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia in southern Spain, home of the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: After company banquet maybe I have livened up

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a banquet is an example of a meal
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone says they perked up after a company dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To come alive is to become lively or animated, which is to liven up.

clue.text: Rome is transformed with introduction of a dictator?

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged
an introduction here is a putting in, so another piece is inserted into the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written
per means a, as in so much a day

explanation.surface: Rome was changed when a dictator was installed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Rome passing from republic to empire under Augustus. Per for a is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor holds absolute power, so he may well be a dictator, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Least clear, opposing a visiting speaker maybe

blocks.note: v is short for versus, against
taken as written
a visiting speaker is an example of a guest

explanation.surface: The most muddled argument comes from a guest speaker taking the opposing side.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague means unclear or imprecise, so the superlative is the most unclear.

clue.text: Queen isn't twee

blocks.note: Qu is a standard abbreviation for queen
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A declaration that the Queen is not sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means old-fashioned in an attractive way, and twee is its over-sweet, chintzy synonym.

clue.text: 18? Peace is truncated by one that's sacked Gaul

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off
a sacked city is plundered and wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: calm is peace and quiet
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calm is cut short by a conqueror who has ravaged Gaul.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 18 down, EMPEROR. The surface suggests a Roman general such as Caesar sacking Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Caligula was the third Roman emperor, an example of the ruler named at 18.

clue.text: Servant absorbing scripture – one laps it up?

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a page is a young servant or attendant
OT is the Old Testament, part of scripture

explanation.surface: A servant soaks up holy writ, eagerly lapping up every word.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'one' as the thing, the soup, that 'it' refers to: what you lap up from a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, something a hungry diner would lap up with a spoon.

clue.text: It's hot in Pacific location – you must discard a bit of clothing

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
discarding means throwing away, so the named letter a is dropped

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Tonga is a Polynesian island kingdom in the Pacific

explanation.surface: It is so hot on a Pacific island that you need to shed some clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy undergarment or swimsuit bottom, a small item of clothing.

clue.text: Dad taking coloured liquid with hesitation, swallowing bad medicine?

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something down inside, so one part is placed within the rest

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
ink is a coloured liquid for writing
ill means bad, as in ill effects
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Father hesitantly swallows a coloured liquid that turns out to be nasty medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three pieces join, and that whole string swallows ILL just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is an analgesic drug, one type of medicine, hence the question mark.

clue.text: German composer's last quartet – it contains some hot stuff?

indicators.note: a quartet is a group of four, and last says it is the four at the end

blocks.note: the final four letters of Beethoven, the German composer

explanation.surface: A remark about the final string quartet written by a German composer, which has some passionate music.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's late string quartets are famous, so 'last quartet' looks musical; it means the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is an enclosed space for cooking or baking, so it holds hot food inside it.

clue.text: Checks car, needing test regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Audi is a make of car
the first and third letters of test

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a car that needs its regular test.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a routine car inspection, such as the British annual MOT test.
explanation.definitionFit: Audits are official examinations, especially of accounts, so they are inspections or checks.

clue.text: Female, just a grotesque person?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
just and right both mean fair

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a woman is merely a grotesque figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but means fair or right.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a fright is someone of shocking or ridiculous appearance, as in 'she looked a fright'.
